```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(framework)
scaffold()
```

This notebook brings the study's raw extracts into the project, registers them
in the data catalog, and builds the analysis dataset the later notebooks use.
Every read and save is tracked by a SHA-256 hash in `framework.db`, and locked
files refuse to load if they change.

## Reading a file directly

`data_read()` takes a plain path too. Here it reads the site list straight from
the shared CSV folder, with no catalog entry. The type comes from the
extension.

```{r}
sites <- data_read("../../shared/csv/sites.csv")
sites
```

## Raw data lands in inputs/raw

A data manager has "delivered" the participant and visit extracts. Copying them
into `inputs/raw/` stands in for that delivery.

```{r}
shared_csv <- "../../shared/csv"
for (file in c("participants.csv", "visits.csv")) {
  file.copy(file.path(shared_csv, file), file.path("inputs/raw", file), overwrite = TRUE)
}
list.files("inputs/raw")
```

`data_add()` registers an existing file. The name comes from the folder
(`inputs/raw/visits.csv` becomes `inputs.raw.visits`), the hash is recorded,
and the entry is written to `settings/data.yml`. Open that file after this
chunk to see it.

```{r}
data_add("inputs/raw/participants.csv")
data_add("inputs/raw/visits.csv")
```

## Browsing the catalog

`data_list()` shows what's registered; `data_info()` shows how one entry will
be read.

```{r}
data_list()
```

```{r}
data_info("inputs.raw.visits")
```

## Reading by name

Once registered, read by dot name instead of path. The hash is checked first
because the entries are locked.

```{r}
visits <- data_read("inputs.raw.visits")
participants <- data_read("inputs.raw.participants")

nrow(visits)
nrow(participants)
```

A quick look at missingness before building anything: visits have gaps in
blood pressure and weight, and some participants lack a BMI.

```{r}
visits |> summarise(across(c(systolic_bp, diastolic_bp, weight_kg), ~ sum(is.na(.x))))
participants |> summarise(missing_bmi = sum(is.na(bmi)))
```

## Locked files catch changes

This copies the site list into `inputs/raw/`, registers it, and then appends a
row behind Framework's back. The next `data_read()` stops with a hash mismatch.

```{r}
file.copy(file.path(shared_csv, "sites.csv"), "inputs/raw/sites.csv", overwrite = TRUE)
data_add("inputs/raw/sites.csv")

cat("5,Hilltop Clinic,Rochester,MN,urban\n", file = "inputs/raw/sites.csv", append = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| error: true
data_read("inputs.raw.sites")
```

`data_verify()` does the same check without reading the data and returns
`TRUE` or `FALSE`, so it suits a pre-flight check in a script.

```{r}
data_verify("inputs.raw.sites")
data_verify("inputs.raw.visits")
```

Restoring the original file makes it pass again.

```{r}
file.copy(file.path(shared_csv, "sites.csv"), "inputs/raw/sites.csv", overwrite = TRUE)
data_verify("inputs.raw.sites")
```

## Saving intermediate data from the database

Lab results come from the shared database. This reshapes them to one row per
visit and saves them with dot notation: `inputs.intermediate.labs_wide`
becomes `inputs/intermediate/labs_wide.rds`, registered and hashed in one step.

```{r}
labs_wide <- db_query("SELECT visit_id, test, value FROM labs", "study") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = test, values_from = value)

data_save(labs_wide, "inputs.intermediate.labs_wide")
```

For a CSV a collaborator can open in a spreadsheet, end the dot name with
`.csv`. `"inputs.final.labs_wide.csv"` is the catalog name
`inputs.final.labs_wide`, saved as `inputs/final/labs_wide.csv`. (`type =
"csv"` does the same.)

```{r}
data_save(labs_wide, "inputs.final.labs_wide.csv")
data_info("inputs.final.labs_wide")$path
```

A plain path also works, starting at the project root wherever you call from.
The hash is recorded but the file isn't added to the catalog, so you read and
verify it by path.

```{r}
data_save(sites, "inputs/intermediate/sites_snapshot.csv")
data_verify("inputs/intermediate/sites_snapshot.csv")
```

## Building the analysis dataset with a script

Repeatable data preparation belongs in `scripts/`. This runs
`scripts/build-analysis-data.R`, which joins visits to participants and sites
and saves `inputs.final.bp_long`. You could also run it from the shell with
`Rscript scripts/build-analysis-data.R`.

```{r}
source("scripts/build-analysis-data.R")
```

```{r}
bp_long <- data_read("inputs.final.bp_long")
glimpse(bp_long)
```

The blood pressure categories come from `classify_bp()` in `functions/`.

```{r}
bp_long |> count(treatment, bp_category) |> tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = treatment, values_from = n)
```

## The catalog now

Everything saved with dot notation is in the catalog, and every save is
recorded in `framework.db`.

```{r}
data_list()
```
